title: Demand-paged page table
purpose: Show resident/absent pages and exact present-bit/frame relationships from original demand-paging example.
requiredChecks: Page table resident rows are 0/A/frame4/1, 2/C/frame6/1, 5/F/frame9/1; rows 1,3,4,6,7 are absent with dash frame and present0.
Physical memory shows frames4:A,6:C,9:F consistently; backing storage includes nonresident B,D,E,G,H.
Legend clearly equates present1 with resident and present0 with not currently resident; all table labels/counts are legible.
alt: Demand paging: pages A, C and F are resident in frames 4, 6 and 9; other pages are nonresident
prompt:
Create a NEW original technical educational diagram for an English operating-systems blog. White background, dark navy crisp sans-serif text, blue and teal flat boxes, clean thin arrows, ample whitespace, large legible labels, no copied textbook artwork, no logos or watermark. TITLE "Demand-paged page table". Wide layout, a readable TABLE on the left with headers exactly "Page", "Contents", "Frame", "Present". Eight rows, exact data:
0 | A | 4 | 1
1 | B | — | 0
2 | C | 6 | 1
3 | D | — | 0
4 | E | — | 0
5 | F | 9 | 1
6 | G | — | 0
7 | H | — | 0.
On right show a box "Physical memory" containing three NON-CONTIGUOUS resident-frame entries "Frame 4: A", "Frame 6: C", "Frame 9: F" and a small label "Other frames omitted" so these are NOT depicted as all physical frames. Below it a box "Backing storage — nonresident pages" with B,D,E,G,H exactly once each. Do not copy cylindrical disk graphics. Legend verbatim "Present 1: resident" and "Present 0: not currently resident". No invented numeric frame mappings. Do not map B,D,E,G,H to RAM. The table itself communicates mapping; no mapping arrows are required, to avoid clutter. Keep all eight rows correct.
